I'm assuming the following: you're using Seedance 2.5 through the standard web or API interface, with image-to-video and multi-image reference input, and the clip is 16:9. Setting names differ between platforms, such as Dreamina/Jimeng, BytePlus ModelArk and third-party hosts, so match my settings to the closest option you have. I couldn't test this exact model version, so treat these as strong defaults and expect to run a few seeds.

## What went wrong

**The face changed into someone else because:**
1. **The model only knew one view of her.** A single photo, probably taken from the front, says nothing about how her face looks in profile or at three-quarters. When she turned, the model had to guess, and it guessed a different person.
2. **"A beautiful woman" pulled toward a generic face.** That phrase points the model at an average "beautiful woman," which competes with your reference photo.
3. **The shot was wide and busy.** In a wide street shot her face is small, so the model has little detail to hold onto. Passersby crossing in front of her break continuity even more.
4. **Too much happened in one clip.** Walking, a head turn, a smile and a moving crowd all compete. Every extra motion makes drift more likely.

**The sign text became gibberish because:**
5. **Video models can't reliably write Armenian script.** They do poorly with non-Latin text, and the letters shift from frame to frame. You can't fix this with prompt wording. Either keep the text out of focus or add real text yourself afterwards.
6. **"cinematic, 4K, IMAX, masterpiece" doesn't help.** Those words don't improve fidelity and use up prompt space. Resolution comes from the settings, not the prompt.

## The fix

- **Split the idea into two shots.** Shot A is the walk, seen from behind or at three-quarters so her face matters little. Shot B is a medium close-up of the turn and smile, where her identity matters most. Cut them together.
- **Give the model 3 reference photos of the actress:** front, three-quarter and profile. Use the same lighting and hairstyle in all three, and match the clip's lighting (warm or neon) if you can.
- **Start Shot B from an image.** Make a first-frame still where she's already looking about 45° away. Either generate it with your reference photos in an image model, or use a real photo. A smaller turn, from 45° to facing the camera instead of 90° to facing the camera, drifts much less.
- **Keep the signs blurred.** Use a shallow depth of field so the neon is soft color and glow. If the Armenian lettering must be readable, add it afterwards in After Effects, Resolve or Fusion: put real text on the out-of-focus signs and blur or glow it to match. If you'd rather not composite, use a real Yerevan street photo as the background of the first frame and keep the camera almost still. The text then mostly holds, but check every frame.
- **Clear the area around her face.** Keep pedestrians thin and soft in the background, and don't let anyone cross in front of her.

## FINAL

**References to upload:**
- `@Image1`: actress facing the camera
- `@Image2`: actress at three-quarter view
- `@Image3`: actress in profile
- For Shot B only, `@Image4`: first-frame still, a medium close-up with her head about 45° away from the camera

---

**SHOT A: the walk (text-to-video plus the identity references)**

Prompt:
```
The woman from @Image1, @Image2 and @Image3 walks away from the camera along a Yerevan street at night, wearing a tailored red wool coat. The camera follows behind her in a slow, steady tracking shot at shoulder height. Neon signs line the street, shown as soft, out-of-focus glows in red, cyan and amber, reflecting on wet cobblestones. A few pedestrians stay in the soft background. Shallow depth of field, 35mm lens, anamorphic bokeh, natural film grain, realistic motion.
```
Negative prompt (if your platform has one):
```
readable text, letters, writing, logos, distorted face, face change, extra people crossing the subject, warping, flicker
```

**SHOT B: the turn and smile (image-to-video, first frame = @Image4)**

Prompt:
```
The woman from @Image1, @Image2 and @Image3 (same face, same identity throughout) stands on a Yerevan street at night in a red wool coat. Medium close-up, face clearly lit. She slowly turns her head from a three-quarter angle toward the camera, makes eye contact, and gives a soft, natural smile. Her features stay consistent throughout the turn. Locked-off camera with a very slight push-in. The background is soft bokeh from neon signs in magenta, cyan and amber, completely out of focus. No pedestrians pass in front of her. Gentle neon rim light on her hair, soft key light on her face, 50mm lens, f/1.8, natural skin texture, film grain.
```
Negative prompt:
```
readable text, letters, signage text, morphing face, different person, identity change, face distortion, asymmetrical eyes, extra teeth, hair covering face, occlusion, flicker
```

---

**Settings (both shots):**

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Mode | A: text-to-video plus references. B: image-to-video (first frame = @Image4) plus references |
| Resolution | 1080p (upscale afterwards if you need 4K) |
| Aspect ratio | 16:9 (use 9:16 for vertical social video) |
| Duration | **5 s** (shorter clips drift less; avoid 10 s for the turn) |
| Motion strength / dynamics | Low to medium (about 0.3–0.4 if it's a slider) |
| Camera | A: tracking/follow. B: fixed or slight push-in |
| Reference strength / face consistency | Highest available |
| Seed | Fixed while you adjust the wording, then try 4–6 seeds and keep the best |
| Prompt extension / "enhance prompt" | **Off** (it adds back generic wording) |
| Audio (if generated natively) | Night city ambience only, no dialogue |

**Post-production:** Cut A into B. If the signs must be readable, track real Armenian text onto the bokeh shapes and add matching blur and glow.
